cohort_definition: US undergraduate Summer Analysts in Morgan Stanley's Investment Banking Division (industry coverage and product groups), penultimate-year students, and the full-time Analyst class they convert into. Experienced hires, MBA Summer Associates, and non-IBD divisions are out of scope.

compensation_notes.note: Official posting states an expected base pay rate of $52.89 per hour at commencement of employment for the 2027 US IBD Summer Analyst role, with total compensation potentially including incentive/discretionary components. Summer pay only; no full-time or bonus figure is published on the posting and none is stated here.

hiring_bar_summary: Firm-published bar for the 2027 US IBD Summer Analyst cohort: undergraduate graduating December 2027–June 2028, minimum 3.4 GPA, basic knowledge of and keen interest in finance, plus analytical ability, teamwork, work ethic/leadership, and strong oral and written communication (official posting, verified 2026-10-12). The 3.4 figure is a stated minimum, not a description of who actually gets interviews; plan as if the effective bar is higher and compensate with experience and networking (agent judgment, labeled).

hiring_cadence.summary: Annual junior-summer cycle with an early calendar: for Summer 2027, US IBD applications ran January 1 – February 15, 2026 on a rolling basis (official posting). Sophomore/early-insight touchpoints run in the fall before (Early Insights sessions Nov 2 and 5, 2026 for the following cycle's sophomores). Dates shift yearly — re-verify each cycle; any date in this record older than 6 months should be treated as a cadence marker, not a deadline.

interview_styles.style: Technical readiness is screened through the stated requirement of basic finance knowledge: expect accounting, three-statement, valuation (DCF/comps) and transaction-reasoning questions. Topic list is a reported recruiting norm for IB interviews generally, not a firm-published syllabus.
Behavioral/fit emphasis on teamwork, leadership, and communication, matching the qualities named on the official posting

known_biases_of_data: Built only from firm-published program/posting material and one university relay of a firm program notice — this describes the stated process, not the revealed preferences of actual hiring, which require population data this record does not have.
No licensed population sample: school, major, and prior-employer distributions are omitted by design rather than estimated.
Syndicated copies of the official posting were used where the firm ATS blocks automated readers; wording was cross-checked between the ATS crawl and the syndicated copy.
Survivorship caveat (Doc 3 §1): even where patterns are described, they show who the process is built for, not the odds for any individual applicant.

major_dist.note: The official US IBD posting does not restrict by major; it asks for basic knowledge of and a keen interest in finance. No major mix of actual hires is published.

path_patterns.pattern: Penultimate-year summer internship in IBD is the firm's stated entry cohort: the 2027 US program is for undergraduates graduating December 2027 to June 2028.

Earlier-stage funnel exists before the junior summer: the firm publicly describes Early Insight and Sophomore Programs ahead of Analyst internships, and ran a virtual Early Insights Program for sophomores (graduating Dec 2028–Jun 2029) with sessions on Nov 2 and Nov 5, 2026.

Reported norm (not firm-published): successful candidates typically stack smaller finance internships (boutique, search fund, corporate finance) in freshman/sophomore summers before the junior-summer seat. This is the Doc 3 §4.1 experience-ladder pattern, labeled as a reported norm.

Interview rounds and a final-round (superday-style) stage — the specific stage sequence for US IBD was not stated on the posting text reviewed; video-interview then interview then superday is the sequence the firm publishes for other campus programs, so treat exact US IBD staging as to-be-confirmed each cycle

Summer program performance, then full-time conversion decision — the summer-to-full-time conversion pattern is the industry structure described in Doc 3 §4.1; the firm does not publish a conversion rate and none is stated here

red_flags: Stale-date risk is the named failure mode here: the Summer 2027 window (Jan 1–Feb 15, 2026) is already closed as of 2026-10-12. Anyone quoting it as 'open' is working from stale data.
The stated 3.4 GPA minimum is a floor for applying, not the competitive bar; treating it as '3.4 is fine' would mislead.
The firm's ATS blocks automated reading (bot check), so posting details can change without this record seeing it — re-verify on the live posting each cycle.
No conversion rate, class size, or school mix is published; any source quoting precise figures for this cohort is not citing the firm.
referral_weight_notes: The firm does not publish referral policy for campus hiring. Reported norm (Doc 3 §4.1, labeled): networking and referrals carry heavy weight in IB recruiting, especially for non-target-school candidates, and the online application alone is a low-odds route. Treat as community-reported practice, not firm policy.

thesis_text: Bottom line: Morgan Stanley IBD's documented front door is the junior-summer analyst program, and its calendar is early — for Summer 2027 the firm took US applications January 1 to February 15, 2026, reviewed on a rolling basis (official posting, verified 2026-10-12). Who gets in, per the firm's own stated screen: penultimate-year undergraduates (graduating Dec 2027–Jun 2028 for that cohort) with at least a 3.4 GPA, basic finance knowledge, and evidence of analytical ability, teamwork, and leadership. What the firm says vs. what to plan for: the 3.4 is a published minimum, and the honest read is that interviews go to candidates who also show the experience ladder — smaller finance internships and finance-club substance from freshman/sophomore years — plus technical readiness in accounting and valuation. Routes in, ranked: (1) the junior-summer IBD application, filed at the very start of the window because review is rolling; (2) sophomore-year positioning — the firm's Early Insights programming for sophomores and sophomore summer roles in adjacent divisions build the resume the junior application is judged on; (3) networking with analysts and associates ahead of the window, which reported IB norms weight heavily, particularly from non-target schools. Key dates to plan around: expect the next junior-summer window to open around the start of the calendar year based on the 2027 cycle's cadence — confirm on the live posting, because the firm moves these dates. Risks and alternatives: missing the short rolling window costs a full year, so the adjacent-division sophomore route and other banks' calendars are the hedge. Offer to execute: build the networking list and a technicals study plan dated against the next window opening.

values_culture_signals.signal: The posting frames the desired hire around integrity and excellence standards and teamwork; summer work is described as functioning like a full-time analyst on live coverage/product teams
